data.hypothesis: Cancelling the target mass algebraically in each interaction should remove a repeated multiply and the final per-target force division while preserving the original self-exclusion and one-target-per-thread loop. This isolates arithmetic from the previously tested split-loop control change; changed rounding and overflow behavior still require controller correctness checks, especially for coincident positions and extreme masses.

transformations: Cancel the target mass from the force-per-target-mass update by accumulating acceleration using source mass directly and removing the final division by target mass.
Retain the original self-interaction exclusion, source loop, and one-target-per-thread execution; make no shared-memory or multi-target changes.
